\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ತೂಗು} (tūgu)}{ತೂಗು (tūgu)}]{\kn{ತೂಗು} (tūgu) — to weigh; to swing}

\label{lesson:KA-C438-tugu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to scan, then the Kannada for a pilot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತೂಗು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತೂಗು}} — \emph{tūgu} — \textquotedblleft{}to weigh; to swing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಸಿಬ್ಬಂದಿ} \kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಸೂಟ್ಕೇಸನ್ನು} \kn{ತೂಗಿದರು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sibbandi nanna sūṭkēsannu tūgidaru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The staff weighed my suitcase.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ತೂಗಿದೆ}, \emph{tūgide}.

The noun beside it is \kn{ತೂಕ}, weight; \kn{ತೊಟ್ಟಿಲು} \kn{ತೂಗು} is to rock a cradle.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ತೂಗು}} (\emph{tūgu}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3376 lists Kannada \emph{tūgu}, \emph{tūṅku}, \textquotedblleft{}to weigh, to swing, to rock a cradle\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūgu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūgu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sibbandi nanna sūṭkēsannu tūgidaru.} — The staff weighed my suitcase.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to scan, then the Kannada for a pilot, then say \emph{tūgu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತೂಗು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To weigh; to swing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಮಿತಿ} (miti)}{ಮಿತಿ (miti)}]{\kn{ಮಿತಿ} (miti) — a limit}

\label{lesson:KA-C438-miti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a pilot, then the Kannada for to weigh.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಮಿತಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಮಿತಿ}} — \emph{miti} — \textquotedblleft{}a limit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಸಾಮಾನಿನ} \kn{ತೂಕಕ್ಕೆ} \kn{ಒಂದು} \kn{ಮಿತಿ} \kn{ಇದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāmānina tūkakke ondu miti ide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a limit on the weight of the luggage.
\end{quote}

\kn{ವೇಗದ} \kn{ಮಿತಿ} is a speed limit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಮಿತಿ}} (\emph{miti}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{miti}, \textquotedblleft{}measuring, measure, weight\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from the root \emph{mā}, \textquotedblleft{}to measure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāmānina tūkakke ondu miti ide.} — There is a limit on the weight of the luggage.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a pilot, then the Kannada for to weigh, then say \emph{miti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಮಿತಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A limit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಮೀರು} (mīru)}{ಮೀರು (mīru)}]{\kn{ಮೀರು} (mīru) — to exceed; to go beyond}

\label{lesson:KA-C438-miru}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to weigh, then the Kannada for a limit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಮೀರು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೀರು}} — \emph{mīru} — \textquotedblleft{}to exceed; to go beyond\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ನನ್ನ} \kn{ಚೀಲದ} \kn{ತೂಕ} \kn{ಮಿತಿಯನ್ನು} \kn{ಮೀರಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nanna cīlada tūka mitiyannu mīritu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weight of my bag went over the limit.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \kn{ಮೀರಿದೆ}, \emph{mīride}.

What is exceeded takes -\kn{ಅನ್ನು}: \kn{ಮಿತಿಯನ್ನು} \kn{ಮೀರು}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಮೀರು}} (\emph{mīru}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 4884 lists Kannada \emph{mīṟu}, \textquotedblleft{}to go beyond, to exceed, to transgress\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīru}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mīru}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nanna cīlada tūka mitiyannu mīritu.} — The weight of my bag went over the limit.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to weigh, then the Kannada for a limit, then say \emph{mīru} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಮೀರು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To exceed; to go beyond\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ} (vimānayāna)}{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ (vimānayāna)}]{\kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ} (vimānayāna) — air travel; aviation}

\label{lesson:KA-C438-vimanayana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a limit, then the Kannada for to exceed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ}}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ}} — \emph{vimānayāna} — \textquotedblleft{}air travel; aviation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ} \kn{ಈಗ} \kn{ಮೊದಲಿಗಿಂತ} \kn{ಅಗ್ಗವಾಗಿದೆ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vimānayāna īga modaliginta aggavāgide.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Air travel is cheaper now than before.
\end{quote}

\kn{ವಿಮಾನ}, an aeroplane, plus \kn{ಯಾನ}, going.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ}} (\emph{vimānayāna}) is built from two Sanskrit words: \emph{vimāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a flying car of the gods\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11823), now an aeroplane, and \emph{yāna}, \textquotedblleft{}going, a vehicle\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10459).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānayāna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānayāna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vimānayāna īga modaliginta aggavāgide.} — Air travel is cheaper now than before.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a limit, then the Kannada for to exceed, then say \emph{vimānayāna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Air travel; aviation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್} (helikāpṭar)}{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್ (helikāpṭar)}]{\kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್} (helikāpṭar) — a helicopter}

\label{lesson:KA-C438-helikaptar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to exceed, then the Kannada for air travel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್}} — \emph{helikāpṭar} — \textquotedblleft{}a helicopter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್} \kn{ಬೆಟ್ಟದ} \kn{ಮೇಲೆ} \kn{ಇಳಿಯಿತು}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{helikāpṭar beṭṭada mēle iḷiyitu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The helicopter landed on the hill.
\end{quote}

\kn{ಇಳಿ}, to get down, also means to land.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಹೆಲಿಕಾಪ್ಟರ್}} (\emph{helikāpṭar}) is a loan from English \emph{helicopter}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{helikāpṭar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{helikāpṭar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{helikāpṭar beṭṭada mēle iḷiyitu.} — The helicopter landed on the hill.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for to exceed, then the Kannada for air travel, then say \emph{helikāpṭar} again
\end{itemize}
